title: Packing extra positionals into *args
blurb: Fixed parameters bind first; everything left over is packed into a tuple.

notes.3: The call starts: 1 -> a, 2 -> b, and 3, 4, 5 are packed into the tuple args.
notes.2: Inside the function: args is a tuple holding every extra positional argument (empty when there are none).
notes.4: Second call with no extras: args is an empty tuple, not an error.

title: Passing a list vs unpacking it with *
blurb: A list passed directly is ONE argument; *L1 spreads it into separate arguments.

notes.4: The call passes the list as one single argument.
notes.2: print shows args and its length – compare the two calls: ONE element (the whole list) vs THREE elements (unpacked).
notes.5: The * operator unpacks the list into three separate positional arguments.

title: Collecting keyword arguments with **kwargs
blurb: Extra keyword arguments are packed into a dictionary.

notes.3: a and b bind to 1 and 2; name and age have no matching parameter, so they go into kwargs.
notes.2: kwargs is a dict: keys are the argument names, values are what was passed (empty if nothing extra).
notes.4: a and b may be passed by keyword; nothing is left over so kwargs is an empty dict.

title: All parameter kinds together
code: print(a, b, args, c, d, kwargs)

notes.3: 1, 2 -> a, b. 3, 4 -> args. c=10 overrides the default. name='Alice' -> kwargs. d keeps 200.
notes.2: Each parameter received exactly the kind of value its position allows.
notes.4: Only the required a and b given: args=(), c=100, d=200, kwargs={}.

title: Keyword-only parameters after *args
blurb: Parameters after *args can only be given by keyword.

notes.3: 10, 20, 30 are swallowed by args; a and b are matched by keyword.
notes.4: Every value is swallowed by *args, so a and b are never given - Python refuses.

title: Multiple return values
blurb: return a, b packs a tuple; the caller can unpack it.

notes.3: The call binds 3 -> a and 4 -> b; the function body runs next.
notes.2: The comma in return builds the tuple (7, 12) and hands it back to the caller.
notes.4: Same call again; this time the caller will unpack the returned tuple into s and p.
